text:
ada: Heads-up — ran into a gateway match collision in prod this morning. Two routes both match the same request and the runtime picked one unpredictably.

mike: Rough, can you paste the two route specs?

ada: Sure, simplified version:
```yaml
- match:
    host: "*.api.redwood.com"
    path: "/v1/*"
  service: token-service

- match:
    host: "payments.api.redwood.com"
    path: "/v1/payments/*"
  service: payments-service
```
The request was to payments.api.redwood.com/v1/payments/charge and it sometimes routed to token-service.

rachel: Oof. That suggests host wildcard vs literal host precedence isn't implemented deterministically, or path specificity is scored wrong.

mike: Do we have a current tie-breaker doc? I thought it was longest path first then host literal > wildcard.

ada: That's what I expected too. But our logs show the token-service route had a lower creation_ts and it won intermittently. Looks like we fall back to insertion order in some code path.

sleeper-bot: lint: route-ambiguous: matched_patterns=2 hosts=["*.api.redwood.com","payments.api.redwood.com"] paths=["/v1/*","/v1/payments/*"] severity=warning

mike: In that case we need a deterministic precedence algorithm and an explicit field to let operators override. Proposal: 1) host specificity (literal > wildcard), 2) path specificity (more literal segments > wildcards), 3) explicit numeric priority, 4) fallback to creation_ts.

rachel: Numeric priority sounds good, but we should make default=0 so we don't change existing behavior unless someone sets it. Also: console/CI should warn on ambiguous matches.

ada: Agreed. Also request: fail the deploy if two routes are exact-ties and neither has nonzero priority, or at least emit an error with a link to the conflicting routes. Silent ambiguity is dangerous (billing/rate-limits could be wrong).

mike: We must consider telemetry and quotas: rate-limit buckets and per-route metrics need to be owned by the effective route. If two routes flip-flop, dashboards will be noisy. We should attach a route_id to every emitted request and surface a sampling trace when a request matched an ambiguous set.

rachel: UX idea: route-creator flow should show a "match preview" where you can paste sample host+path and it highlights which route wins and why (host vs path vs priority). Also a checkbox "reject ambiguous matches" for stricter teams.

ada: Implementation note: in runtime matcher we already compute a score obj for host/path. Add priority into the score vector and sort by tuple (host_score, path_score, priority, -creation_ts). This keeps it stable and deterministic.

mike: Backcompat check: default priority=0 maintains current ordering except creation_ts used as final tie-breaker. But we should not rely on creation_ts if the operator sets priority explicitly.

deploy-bot: deploy failed: gateway:validation: ambiguous-match detected between routes r_2345 and r_9783. See /deploys/1751234567 for details.

ada: I'll open a small RFC + patch. Draft PR: https://git.company.internal/redwood/gateway/pull/3184 — adds priority field to route schema, console warnings, and a small unit test for tie-breaker.

rachel: Nice. Also add audit log entries when priority is set/changed and when an ambiguity is detected at runtime (sampled).

mike: Can someone own the runtime change? I can take match ordering and unit tests. Ada can take console previews and warnings. Rachel, can you spec the audit/telemetry?

ada: I'll start a branch and drop the YAML schema change in the PR. Thanks, all. :+1:
